6th National Pharmacovigilance Week Celebrated at MGIMS, Sevagram
Friday, 25 September 2026
157 Hits
The Department of Pharmacology, Mahatma Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences (MGIMS), Sevagram, organized the 6th National Pharmacovigilance Week 2026 from 17th to 23rd September 2026 with the theme of promoting safe and rational use of medicines, pharmacovigilance, materiovigilance, and patient safety.
The week-long programme aimed to create awareness among healthcare professionals, students, nursing staff, patients, and the community regarding the importance of identifying, documenting, and reporting adverse drug reactions and medical device-related adverse events. The programme commenced with an inauguration ceremony at S. N. Hall. Dr. Poonam Shivkumar Verma addressed the gathering on patient safety and shared her clinical experiences related to adverse drug reactions in gynaecological patients. An interactive quiz was also organized for second-year nursing students.
Various academic and awareness activities were conducted throughout the week. Sessions on rational use of medicines and pharmacovigilance and hospital device and equipment safety were conducted for students and healthcare professionals. A sensitization programme on pharmacovigilance and materiovigilance was also organized for Second MBBS students. Patient awareness activities were conducted in different OPDs to educate patients and their relatives about the safe use of medicines and the importance of reporting suspected adverse drug reactions. Students also participated in poster-making and pencil-drawing activities to communicate messages related to medication safety and pharmacovigilance through creative means.
A Walkathon titled “Walk for Rational Medicine – Walk for Patient Safety” was organized on September 21. The walk commenced from the Department of Pharmacology and covered various clinical departments and OPDs, including Microbiology, Medicine, Paediatrics, Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Drug Store, Ophthalmology, Surgery, General OPD, Orthopaedics, and Physiotherapy, and concluded at the Dean’s Office. The activity highlighted the importance of rational medicine use, ADR reporting, and collective responsibility for patient safety. A poster presentation was also conducted as part of the programme.
As part of the outreach activities, a sensitization programme was conducted at Civil Hospital, Wardha, extending the message of pharmacovigilance to healthcare professionals outside the institute. On the concluding day, a sensitization session was conducted at the Institute of Pharmaceutical Education and Research (IPER) by Dr. Swamy Bandi, Pharmacovigilance Associate, and Ms. Priyanka Mandal, Materiovigilance Associate.
The Valedictory Function was held in the presence of Dean Dr. A. K. Shukla and Additional Medical Superintendent Dr. Ramesh Pande. The dignitaries appreciated the efforts of the Department of Pharmacology in organizing the week-long programme and emphasized the importance of maintaining a strong culture of patient safety and reporting of adverse events. The programme was conducted under the guidance of Dr. Devesh Gosavi, Professor and Head, Department of Pharmacology and PvPI Coordinator, with the active involvement of Dr. Leena Chimurkar, Deputy Coordinator, Pharmacovigilance; Dr. Ranjana Kale, Materiovigilance Coordinator; Dr. Mohan Pethe, Deputy Coordinator, Materiovigilance; Dr. Swamy Bandi, Pharmacovigilance Associate; Ms. Priyanka Mandal, Materiovigilance Associate, along with  Senior residents,junior residents, , nursing staff, students, and other members of the department.
The celebration concluded with a renewed commitment to promoting rational medicine use, adverse event reporting, medical device safety, and patient safety as a shared responsibility among all healthcare stakeholders.
